Normal car, forward, panto at 6 blocks height.

The MI09 trains are the latest generation serving Paris's busiest RER A line, entering service from 2011 onwards with their distinctive silver white. These double-decker trainsets were specifically designed to handle the large passenger loads of Europe's busiest rail line, carrying more than 2000 passengers per train. It features wide doors for rapid boarding, improved accessibility with dedicated spaces for wheelchairs and bicycles, and modern air conditioning throughout. The TGV Postal was introduced in 1984 and is instantly recognizable by its bright yellow La Poste livery. Based on modified TGV Sud-Est (PSE) units, the postal variants had their passenger compartments replaced with spacious cargo areas capable of holding up to 100 tons of mail and parcels. Operating primarily on overnight routes between Paris and Lyon , they could reach speeds of 270 km/h, dramatically cutting delivery times. For three decades, these specialized trains silently whisked letters and packages across France until changing postal needs led to their retirement in 2015.
